questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to stay in the EU. Wanted a good academic school, and a country that had the similar values/culture as my home country.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: It was  nice with the emails the receiving university and my home university would send with information. questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Urban economics and real estate, data science and visualization in R, empirical economics, solutions to sustainability

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Urban economics and real estate, data science and visualization in R. 

Urban economics and real estate is great if you are interested in economics. The course is an applied course in mireocenomics. 

data science and visualization in R: great for anyone interested in coding and visualizing. if you have worked with R/coding before, then this course is quite easy, but still very usefull sine you learn more about how to visualize data in the best way

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy since NL culture is similar to danish culture. I had to adopt more to my flat mates who were primarily from the UK in Canada.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you live at uilenstede then you should go to il' cafe on fridays / saturdays. You are more likely to meet some dutch people here and they are more talkative under the influence (just like in Denmark):)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Did not find any cultural challenges with dutch people. 
Mostly found differences with my flatmates from the UK and Canada. Everyone on exchange is in general a bit younger than the danish people. Sometimes i felt people where very dramatic and a bit childish and i didn't no if this was due to cultural differences or immaturity. 
My advice is just to be openminded. Everyone you meet doesn't have to become a best friend. Take it as a learning experience to meet people you don't agree with or dont share the same values as.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Drinking the small dutch beers while eating bitterballen

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: In general you should be openminded to meet new people and try new experiences. Exchange can be lonely at times and you need to make an effort to have fun plans and meet good friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting friend from my flat

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Becoming friends with someone I at first could not stand. But because i was openminded i got to know them better and valued our friendship in other ways than what my friendships in Denmark are like.
